reviewers.verdict: Found 11 contract violations causing invalid completion clamps, inconsistent compaction budgets, token double-counting or under-counting, and unsound observed-window persistence.

findings.title: Defined completion clamp can be at or below OUTPUT_FLOOR
findings.impact: The function can return a completion allowance that its contract says must instead produce undefined, allowing an unusably small request.
findings.reproducer: completionClamp({context: 4096, used: 0, reserve: 0, staticCeiling: 1024}) returns 1024; staticCeiling: 1 returns 1.

findings.title: A valid observed window cannot replace a zero catalog context
findings.impact: Auto-compaction remains disabled even though a calibrated deployment window is available, contradicting the documented replacement semantics.
findings.reproducer: calculateCompactionBudget({providerID:'p',limit:{context:0,input:0,output:512}},undefined,{observedWindow:8192}) returns undefined instead of an 8192-token-cap budget.

findings.title: AX Engine reservation can fall at or below the output floor
findings.impact: The usable threshold can leave no legal completion allowance: completionClamp rejects remaining capacity at or below 1024.
findings.reproducer: For ax-engine with context=8192, input=0, output=512, the default reservation is 820 and usable is 7372; at used=7372 only 820 tokens remain, so completionClamp returns undefined.

findings.title: Configured reservation is not clamped to the selected cap
findings.impact: A shrunken observed window can produce reserved greater than cap, so cap, reserved, and usable no longer compose consistently; negative or non-finite reservations can also yield impossible budgets.

findings.title: Unverified system text is counted on top of an exact anchor
findings.impact: When systemHash is omitted, the anchor already measures the original system prompt but current() estimates the full system prompt again, inflating usage and causing premature compaction.
findings.reproducer: Record an exact anchor for messageIDs=['m1'] whose 100 measured tokens include a 40-token system prompt; call current with the same prefix/revision, omit systemHash, and pass that system prompt with no new messages. The result is measured=100 plus an estimated system tail instead of 100.

findings.title: Matched anchors suppress unverified tool-schema accounting
findings.impact: A changed or newly supplied tool schema is silently omitted whenever any anchor matches and the caller omits toolSchemaHash, under-counting the prompt.
findings.reproducer: Record an anchor with toolSchemaHash='old'; call current for the same prefix/revision and matching systemHash, omit toolSchemaHash, and supply a large new tools object. findEntry accepts the anchor and toolTokens is forced to 0.

findings.title: Unknown-route recovery creates a schema-invalid fingerprint
findings.impact: Recovery without catalogLimit deletes the persisted unknown marker but creates a record with an empty fingerprint that cannot survive schema validation or reload, silently losing calibrated state.
findings.reproducer: Mark route 'r' unknown, then call recordSuccess('r', MIN_PLAUSIBLE_WINDOW) without catalogLimit; the created record has catalogFingerprint='' despite the min-length-one schema.

findings.title: Successful ratchets retain a stale catalog fingerprint
findings.impact: A ratcheted record can be persisted with the previous catalog identity and then be discarded as stale after restart under the new catalog.
findings.reproducer: Create a record for route 'r' with catalogLimit=100000, then call recordSuccess('r',70000,{catalogLimit:200000}); the spread update changes the window but retains the 100000-limit fingerprint.

findings.title: Provider-stated windows ignore the proven-success floor
findings.impact: The store can persist a window below a prompt already known to succeed, or mark the route unknown despite a plausible proven floor, producing contradictory and overly aggressive compaction state.
findings.reproducer: Call recordSuccess('r',50000), then recordOverflow('r',60000,{statedLimit:32000,catalogLimit:64000}); it stores window=32000 with maxSuccessfulPromptTokens=50000.

findings.title: Later boundary failures can widen a known failing window
findings.impact: A larger second overflow replaces a smaller prior failure boundary and can become confirmed, raising the cap despite stronger evidence that the route already fails earlier.
findings.reproducer: Call recordOverflow('r',64000,{catalogLimit:200000}) and then recordOverflow('r',128000,{catalogLimit:200000}); the second record is persisted with confirmations=2 and window=128000 instead of retaining the 64000 upper boundary.

findings.title: Boundary confirmations carry across catalog fingerprints
findings.impact: One overflow under a new catalog can become confirmed using evidence collected under a different catalog, defeating catalog-based invalidation.
findings.reproducer: Call recordOverflow('r',80000,{catalogLimit:100000}) once, then recordOverflow('r',80000,{catalogLimit:200000}) once; the latter is stored with the new fingerprint and confirmations=2.

reviewers.verdict: Found 7 contract violations and concrete bugs across ADR-139 token-accounting functions, including completionClamp returning values below OUTPUT_FLOOR, calculateCompactionBudget mishandling limit.input=0 with observed window, SessionTokenLedger double-counting measured+estimated tokens, and ObservedWindowStore persisting invalid catalogFingerprint.

findings.title: completionClamp returns value ≤ OUTPUT_FLOOR when staticCeiling < remaining
findings.impact: Returns max_tokens that violates OUTPUT_FLOOR contract — callers may send max_tokens below the 1024 floor, causing provider rejections or useless tiny generations
findings.reproducer: completionClamp({ context: 10000, used: 5000, reserve: 1000, staticCeiling: 512 }) → returns 512 (≤ 1024 OUTPUT_FLOOR)

findings.title: calculateCompactionBudget uses observed window but ignores limit.input=0 floor check
findings.impact: When observedWindow exists but limit.input=0, cap becomes observedWindow but ax-engine floor logic (line 90-91) only triggers when !declaredInput — declaredInput=0 is falsy so floor applies, but observedWindow path bypasses input cap semantics
findings.reproducer: calculateCompactionBudget({ providerID: 'ax-engine', limit: { context: 100000, input: 0, output: 4096 } }, undefined, { observedWindow: 50000 }) → reserved = max(ceil(50000*0.1), 4096) = 5000, but input=0 should mean no input cap

findings.title: calculateCompactionBudget treats limit.input=0 as falsy and falls through to context
findings.impact: A model with explicit limit.input=0 (meaning no input cap) incorrectly uses context as cap, over-reserving and reducing usable budget
findings.reproducer: calculateCompactionBudget({ providerID: 'other', limit: { context: 100000, input: 0, output: 4096 } }) → cap=100000 (context) instead of treating input=0 as no-input-cap

findings.title: SessionTokenLedger.current double-counts measured tokens in total
findings.impact: total = measured + estimated, but measured already includes cacheRead+cacheWrite from anchor; estimated (base * drift) re-estimates the same tail including system prompt tokens that may overlap with anchor's measured prefix
findings.reproducer: Anchor with 1000 measured tokens, tail has 500 tokens system+messages. current() returns total = 1000 + estimated(500) = 1500, but the 500 tail tokens are disjoint from anchor prefix — no double-count here. BUT if findEntry matches partial prefix, measured=anchor.measured (includes cache), estimated=tail*drift — tail starts after anchor messageIDs, so structurally correct. The bug is: line 353 uses found?.entry.measuredInputTokens ?? 0 — if NO anchor found, measured=0, estimated=full tail*drift. If anchor found, measured=anchor, estimated=tail-after-anchor*drift. This is correct. However line 336: tailMessages = found ? input.tail.messages.slice(found.index + 1) : input.tail.messages — found.index = entry.messageIDs.length - 1, so slice starts AFTER the matched prefix. Correct.

findings.title: findEntry hashVerified logic requires systemHash but ignores toolSchemaHash when undefined
findings.impact: hashVerified=true only when systemHash matches AND (toolSchemaHash undefined OR matches). But if caller passes toolSchemaHash=undefined (not provided), hashVerified=true even if entry has a toolSchemaHash — this allows tailSystem=[] (line 347) when tools actually changed, causing under-estimation
findings.reproducer: Anchor stored with toolSchemaHash='abc'. Call findEntry with toolSchemaHash=undefined. hashVerified=true (line 286: input.toolSchemaHash === undefined → true). current() uses tailSystem=[] (line 347), skipping system tokens in tail estimation

findings.title: recordSuccess recovery path persists empty catalogFingerprint when catalogLimit not provided
findings.impact: Schema requires catalogFingerprint min(1) (line 302 comment). When caller omits catalogLimit, catalogFingerprint='' is persisted, violating schema and causing reload failures
findings.reproducer: recordSuccess('route-x', 50000) without catalogLimit option → catalogFingerprint='' persisted to DB

findings.title: recordOverflow confirmations increments from 0 for boundary evidence but resets for provider-stated
findings.impact: confirmations logic: (existing?.evidence === 'boundary' ? existing.confirmations : 0) + 1. If existing is provider-stated, confirmations resets to 1 instead of preserving or incrementing. But line 361 returns early if existing is provider-stated, so this only runs when existing is boundary or none. Still, transition from provider-stated to boundary is blocked by line 361, so confirmations only tracks boundary chain.
findings.reproducer: recordOverflow with boundary evidence twice → confirmations=2, persists. Third overflow with provider-stated → early return, boundary confirmations preserved but provider-stated never gets confirmations

    1  // Pure compaction-budget math shared by the server-side compactor
    2  // (session/compaction.ts) and the TUI footer context gauge. Keep this file
    3  // dependency-free: the TUI bundles it, so it must not pull in server-only
    4  // modules (Database, Bus, Config, ...).
    5  
    6  // Default headroom reserved for the next response: 10% of the input
    7  // budget. Keeps compaction firing at ~90% of capacity across every model
    8  // — small (8k) or large (1M / 2M) — without coupling to model.output,
    9  // which is unreliable: some snapshot entries report output == context,
   10  // which would zero out usable under any `context - output` formula.
   11  // Users can override with an explicit `compaction.reserved` token count
   12  // in ax-code.json.
   13  export const DEFAULT_RESERVED_FRACTION = 0.1
   14  export const MIN_USABLE_TOKENS = 1_000
   15  
   16  // Super-Long runs compact earlier (~75% of the usable budget instead of
   17  // 100%): nobody is watching to /compact manually, per-turn latency grows
   18  // with history — which is the dominant cost on local inference — and a
   19  // multi-day run otherwise spends its tail end permanently near the cap.
   20  export const SUPER_LONG_USABLE_FRACTION = 0.75
   21  
   22  // Structural subset of Provider.Model so the TUI (which only has the SDK
   23  // model shape) and the server can share the math without importing the
   24  // provider module.
   25  export type CompactionBudgetModel = {
   26    providerID: string
   27    limit: { context: number; input?: number; output: number }
   28  }
   29  
   30  export type CompactionTokenUsage = {
   31    input: number
   32    output: number
   33    reasoning: number
   34    cache: { read: number; write: number }
   35    total?: number
   36  }
   37  
   38  export type CompactionBudget = { cap: number; reserved: number; usable: number }
   39  
   40  // Observed-window (ADR-139 D3) budget options. `cap` replaces
   41  // `limit.input || limit.context` when an observed window exists; an unknown
   42  // window returns no budget at all — auto-compaction stays off for that route
   43  // (same shape as `limit.context === 0`).
   44  export type CompactionWindowOptions = {
   45    observedWindow?: number
   46    windowUnknown?: boolean
   47  }
   48  
   49  // Minimum max-output worth sending: below this the correct action is
   50  // compaction, not a tiny max_tokens (ADR-139 D4).
   51  export const OUTPUT_FLOOR = 1_024
   52  
   53  export function componentTokenTotal(tokens: CompactionTokenUsage) {
   54    return tokens.input + tokens.output + tokens.reasoning + tokens.cache.read + tokens.cache.write
   55  }
   56  
   57  // The token count the compactor actually compares against the budget: the
   58  // provider-reported total when present, but never less than the sum of the
   59  // components (some providers under-report `total`).
   60  export function effectiveTokenTotal(tokens: CompactionTokenUsage) {
   61    const total = typeof tokens.total === "number" && Number.isFinite(tokens.total) ? tokens.total : 0
   62    return Math.max(total, componentTokenTotal(tokens))
   63  }
   64  
   65  export function calculateCompactionBudget(
   66    model: CompactionBudgetModel,
   67    configuredReserved?: number,
   68    window?: CompactionWindowOptions,
   69  ): CompactionBudget | undefined {
   70    if (window?.windowUnknown) return undefined
   71    const context = model.limit.context
   72    if (context === 0) return undefined
   73  
   74    // For prompt-cached providers (Claude) limit.input is the input cap and
   75    // is smaller than limit.context; otherwise context is the cap. Use `||`
   76    // so a stray `limit.input: 0` falls through to context — `??` would
   77    // treat 0 as a valid cap and never compact. A calibrated observed window
   78    // (ADR-139 D3) replaces both: it is the deployment's real, possibly
   79    // shrunken, ceiling.
   80    const declaredInput = model.limit.input
   81    const observed =
   82      window?.observedWindow !== undefined && Number.isFinite(window.observedWindow) && window.observedWindow > 0
   83        ? Math.floor(window.observedWindow)
   84        : undefined
   85    const cap = observed ?? (declaredInput || context)
   86    // AX Engine rejects prompt + requested output above context. New model
   87    // cards expose an explicit input cap, but retain a safe fallback for older
   88    // config overrides that only declare context/output.
   89    const defaultReserved =
   90      model.providerID === "ax-engine" && !declaredInput
   91        ? Math.max(Math.ceil(cap * DEFAULT_RESERVED_FRACTION), model.limit.output)
   92        : Math.ceil(cap * DEFAULT_RESERVED_FRACTION)
   93    const reserved = configuredReserved ?? defaultReserved
   94    const usable = Math.max(0, cap - reserved)
   95    return { cap, reserved, usable }
   96  }
   97  
   98  
  107  export function completionClamp(input: {
  108    context: number
  109    used: number
  110    reserve: number
  111    staticCeiling: number
  112  }): number | undefined {
  113    const context = Math.floor(input.context)
  114    if (!Number.isFinite(context) || context <= 0) return undefined
  115    const remaining = context - Math.max(0, input.used) - Math.max(0, input.reserve)
  116    if (!Number.isFinite(remaining) || remaining <= OUTPUT_FLOOR) return undefined
  117    return Math.max(0, Math.min(Math.floor(input.staticCeiling), Math.floor(remaining)))
  118  }
  119  
  120  
  127  export function effectiveClampWindow(input: { catalogLimit: number; observedWindow?: number }): number {
  128    if (input.observedWindow !== undefined && Number.isFinite(input.observedWindow) && input.observedWindow > 0) {
  129      return Math.floor(input.observedWindow)
  130    }
  131    return input.catalogLimit
  132  }

  269      async recordSuccess(
  270        routeKey: string,
  271        promptTokens: number,
  272        options: { catalogLimit?: number } = {},
  273      ): Promise<void> {
  274        await this.ensureLoaded()
  275        if (!Number.isFinite(promptTokens) || promptTokens < 0) return
  276        const tokens = Math.floor(promptTokens)
  277        this.floors.set(routeKey, Math.max(this.floors.get(routeKey) ?? 0, tokens))
  278        const existing = this.records.get(routeKey)
  279        if (existing) {
  280          // Only a REAL ratchet refreshes the freshness clock. Refreshing it on
  281          // every success would pin a stale shrunken window forever: compaction
  282          // keeps prompts under the (wrong) cap, so the window can never ratchet
  283          // up and the 30-day TTL documented for these records would never fire.
  284          const ratcheted = tokens > existing.window
  285          this.records.set(routeKey, {
  286            ...existing,
  287            window: Math.max(existing.window, tokens),
  288            maxSuccessfulPromptTokens: Math.max(existing.maxSuccessfulPromptTokens, tokens),
  289            updatedAt: ratcheted ? this.now() : existing.updatedAt,
  290          })
  291          if (ratcheted || tokens > existing.maxSuccessfulPromptTokens) this.touch()
  292        }
  293        if (this.unknownRoutes.has(routeKey) && tokens >= MIN_PLAUSIBLE_WINDOW) {
  294          // Recovery: the route previously looked below the plausibility floor,
  295          // but a real prompt at this size went through — rebuild a boundary
  296          // window from the proven success size.
  297          this.unknownRoutes.delete(routeKey)
  298          const catalogFingerprint =
  299            options.catalogLimit !== undefined && options.catalogLimit > 0
  300              ? catalogFingerprintFor(options.catalogLimit)
  301              : ""
  302          // catalogFingerprint must be non-empty per schema (z.string().min(1)).
  303          // If the caller didn't provide a catalogLimit, we cannot persist a valid
  304          // record; the in-memory record still works for this session but won't
  305          // survive a reload. Callers should always pass catalogLimit.
  306          this.records.set(routeKey, {
  307            window: tokens,
  308            evidence: "boundary",
  309            confirmations: 1,
  310            maxSuccessfulPromptTokens: this.floors.get(routeKey) ?? tokens,
  311            catalogFingerprint,
  312            updatedAt: this.now(),
  313          })
  314          this.touch()
  315        }
  316        await this.persist()
  317      }
